1.explanation: 1. We launch Puppeteer and navigate to the audited page. 2. We select all `` elements missing both width and height attributes (the same ones the Lighthouse CLS-audit flags). 3. We take a single full-page screenshot (fpss). 4. For each failing image, we compute its on-screen bounding box, crop that region out of the fpss, resize to a thumbnail width (e.g. 200px), then encode as a `data:image/jpeg;base64,……` URI. 5. Finally we emit an `` tag that embeds the thumbnail locally, illustrating how to avoid any remote hot-linking of the original `src` URL.
1.bug_scenario: When running the "Image elements do not have explicit width and height" audit on a live site, Lighthouse’s report currently renders each failing `` tag by simply embedding the page’s real `src` URL inside the report. In other words the report’s HTML contains `` (and others), which means the report hot-links back to the original server for each thumbnail. This breaks CSP/mixed-content if the report is served over HTTPS and leaks requests to remote servers. The goal is to replace those external `` tags with locally‐generated thumbnails extracted from the full-page screenshot (fpss) and embedded as `data:image/...` URIs so that no remote requests are made.
